key_insight: Explicitly enforcing permutation equivariance over symbols in Recurrent Reasoning Models (RRMs) lets the model natively respect symbol symmetries, removing the need for costly data augmentation and yielding more data-efficient, symmetry-aware reasoning.
problem_solved: Neural reasoning models (e.g., HRM, TRM) currently rely on heavy data augmentation to handle interchangeable symbols; this is inefficient and limits generalization on structured reasoning tasks like Sudoku and ARC-AGI.
method: Design SE-RRMs by introducing architectural constraints that enforce permutation equivariance across symbol identities inside the RRM family.
Replace or augment standard message-passing/recurrence with symmetry-aware (equivariant) operations so representations transform consistently under symbol permutations.
Integrate equivariant modules into existing HRM/TRM workflows so compact recurrent reasoning architectures can learn without manual augmentation of symbol permutations.
impact: SE-RRMs reduce reliance on augmentation and improve sample efficiency and robustness for symbolic reasoning tasks, enabling practitioners to train smaller, more generalizable models for structured problem solving.
